title: The Handshake (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist social observation
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The handshake is a thing I learned from watching other men
I wasn't born knowing how to do it — no one was back then
My father's handshake was a thing of measured structural intent
Two pumps, straight grip, eye contact — that's what a handshake meant

[Pre-Chorus]
Then sometime in the nineties several variations arrived
The fist bump, the elaborate thumb thing — I barely survived

[Chorus]
The handshake knows something I don't know
It knows the first impression in the pressure of a hold
The handshake tells you everything before a word is said
Too firm means something, too soft means something — nothing goes ahead
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
I've met men with handshakes like a wet and thoughtful fish
And men with grips so strong they nearly turn your hand to dish
The perfect handshake sits exactly in between
Enough to say I'm here without becoming a scene

[Bridge]
COVID interrupted the whole handshake ceremony
For a year or two the elbow came and then the ceremony
Returned and nobody remembered what they used to do
We all stood there with our hands out — slightly confused too

[Outro]
Handshake knows… first impression before the sentence… handshake knows
That's my boy
